meta.server: Oracle Cloud VM.Standard.E2.4: AMD EPYC 7551 (Zen 1, AVX2, no AVX-512), 8 vCPU = 4 cores x 2 threads (sibling pairs 0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7), 32 GB, KVM, us-ashburn-1
meta.stack: voice service image 1.49.0; local-llm ollama/ollama:0.40.6 (llama-server) qwen2.5:1.5b q4_K_M, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1, flash attention on, batch 512, context 4096, prompt cache 256 MiB; local-tts Pocket TTS 3.3.0 (1 torch thread, voice alba); speech-to-text: the organisation's choice during this work, Whisper small.en via local-speech (speaches 0.8.3, int8, 4 threads) - not changed here
meta.caller: infra/scripts/e2e_test_call.py inside the voice-runtime container (direct host path), 4 caller lines from WAV files made once by Pocket TTS (voice marius) and reused in every run, 15 s between calls; remote run: same script and WAVs on a Windows PC over the internet through the TURN relay
meta.lock: every benchmark ran inside flock /tmp/atlas-bench.lock; another agent's speech-to-text evaluations ran between them, never during
meta.timing: per turn, ms after the caller's last speech frame was sent: stt_final = final transcript event received; llm_start = LLM request sent (ttfb event - ttfb); llm_first = first token; tts_start = first sentence handed to TTS; tts_chunk = first 0.5 s of audio received by the voice service; bot_started = voice service started sending audio; heard = first agent audio frame at or above -45 dBFS at the caller. 'clean' turns exclude the ones where speech-to-text split a caller line in two, which shifts the voice service's events by one turn
meta.tools: infra/scripts/e2e_test_call.py plus analysis scripts kept outside the repository (per-turn waterfall from events.jsonl; LLM turns through Ollama /api/chat with the demo agent's real first request; Pocket TTS streaming timing)

result.note: The whole reply time is dominated by speech-to-text (Whisper small.en, 4.7-4.9 s p50 after the caller stops), owned by another workstream. Everything after the transcript went from 3.0 s to 1.9 s (p50) and 4.0 s to 2.8 s (p90).

llm.threads_batch: llama-server in ollama 0.40.6 reads LLAMA_ARG_THREADS but has no environment variable for --threads-batch (llama-server --help lists none; LLAMA_ARG_THREADS_BATCH=8 left system_info at n_threads_batch = 4). Ollama passes no -t/-tb unless a model sets num_thread.
llm.prompt_cache_in_calls: per turn 95-98 % of the prompt came from the slot (cached n_tokens), 12-40 new tokens read in 0.4-1.9 s; the warm-up at session start re-read 41-200 tokens; after a long reply (167 tokens) that the caller talked over, the next request re-read 167 tokens (5.2 s first token)
llm.post_call_requests: after each call the voice service sends a 470-810 token request with only 263-312 tokens cached: 5.5-8.1 s of all LLM threads, and twice in the final run it was cut off at 10 s (HTTP 500). It would delay a second caller's reply on this server.
llm.temperature: the voice service's requests reach llama-server with temp = 1.000 (llama-server log); ATLAS does not expose a temperature for the model choice although the runtime supports one (vendor service_factory.py:1256-1263)
llm.num_predict: not changed: a cap does not shorten the first sentence and would cut long replies mid-sentence
